title: IPC session.losses result
description: The broadcasts this data connection's session has lost since it opened (IPC 2.11, ADR-0026 A 2026-10-24): two monotonic counts that never fall while the connection lives. queue_overflow counts copies the session's own queue dropped -- its oldest, to take a newer one -- or could not queue; ingress_refused counts broadcasts the ingress gate refused (over the publisher's rate, or while draining) on a channel the session held at the time, since that join. Neither counts what GossipSub dropped before admission (validation, mesh, the backend's queue) or a conflicting body, so zero means none counted, not none lost. The two differ: an overflowed broadcast was admitted and its dedup entry recorded, so within the dedup window a republish of the same id is a duplicate and queue_overflow is a lower bound on broadcasts lost; a refused broadcast was never admitted and has no dedup entry, so a republish may still arrive and each refused copy counts -- ingress_refused is a signal that broadcasts on the session's channels were refused, never a count of distinct broadcasts lost. No peer and no channel is named. Params: the empty object.

queue_overflow.description: Copies this session's queue dropped or could not queue, since it opened.

ingress_refused.description: Copies the ingress gate refused on a channel this session held, since each join; a republish of a refused id may still arrive, and each refused copy counts.
